script:
Good morning, Shahriaar. Today is Sunday, November 22. This is your morning brief.

Weather today is 9 degrees Celsius, overcast. The high will be 18 and the low 9 degrees Celsius. Chance of precipitation is 3 percent.

You have no appointments scheduled in the next 24 hours.

Now, the top 5 stories in AI today.

First, from TechCrunch: Top AI Agents That Can Live in Your Text Messages. A roundup of notable AI agents operating within SMS and messaging platforms, spanning general assistants to specialized agents for family coordination, travel planning, and work tasks. These agents bring autonomous AI capabilities directly into everyday text conversations without requiring separate apps or interfaces. The development signals a shift toward embedding AI agents in existing communication channels, making autonomous task execution more accessible to consumers and workers. Why it matters: Represents practical deployment of AI agents in a ubiquitous interface, potentially changing how businesses and individuals delegate tasks to AI.

Second, from The Verge: Anthropic Goes Public Amid AI Safety Questions. Anthropic, the AI laboratory behind Claude, went public on the Nasdaq. The company is grappling with balancing AI safety priorities against the pressures of being a public company with gigantic financial figures. The IPO represents a major milestone for one of the leading frontier AI labs and raises questions about whether safety-first AI development can survive public market pressures. Why it matters: Anthropic is a top-tier AI company; its public offering and safety posture have broad implications for the AI industry's commercial and ethical direction.

Third, from WIRED: AI-Driven Outages and Cybersecurity Pressures Mount. AI is accelerating the pace at which companies must patch systems, as attackers race to exploit newly discovered vulnerabilities. The article warns of increasing internet outage chaos driven by AI-enabled attack speeds and defensive patching demands. Enterprises face growing pressure to update infrastructure rapidly or risk disruption, signaling a new era of AI-driven cyber instability. Why it matters: Directly affects enterprise IT and security planning, highlighting AI's dual role in creating and responding to infrastructure vulnerabilities.

Fourth, from TechCrunch: A Tale of Two Nvidias. Nvidia's latest earnings report presents one picture of the company, while tech executives are publicly calling for CEO Jensen Huang's return, suggesting a divergent narrative around leadership and performance. The piece contrasts financial results with executive sentiment regarding Nvidia's central role in AI hardware and the broader AI infrastructure market. As a dominant supplier of AI chips, Nvidia's stability and leadership are closely watched across the technology sector. Why it matters: Nvidia is foundational to AI infrastructure; leadership and market perceptions around the company affect the broader AI supply chain.

Fifth, from TechCrunch: Signal Restricts Mobile Screenshots Over AI Surveillance. Signal is restricting screenshot functionality on both Android and iOS apps as it confronts what it describes as an existential threat from AI surveillance. The move aims to protect user privacy against AI-powered monitoring and screen capture threats, reflecting growing tension between secure messaging and artificial intelligence capabilities. The feature limitation underscores how AI surveillance is forcing privacy-focused platforms to alter core user functionality. Why it matters: Highlights escalating privacy threats from AI surveillance and how secure communication platforms are adapting product features in response.

That is your brief. Have a great day.
